messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Testing the BACI interaction in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Gretchen,

This is specific to linear modeling in R.  In your other model runs, you removed the intercepts to obtain a means parameterization instead of an effects parameterization.  You can't obtain a means parameterization when you have an interaction with >1 factor, unless you coded your covariates to be a single factor with 4 levels (and removed the intercept). 

If you look at my example code below, you can see how your design matrix is set up under the formula you used:

df <- expand.grid(hvst=factor(c("pre","post")),trt=factor(c("Con","Trt")))

  hvst trt
1  pre Con
2 post Con
3  pre Trt
4 post Trt

model.matrix(~hvst*trt,df)

  (Intercept) hvstpre trtTrt hvstpre:trtTrt
1           1       1      0              0
2           1       0      0              0
3           1       1      1              1
4           1       0      1              0

For each of the 4 combinations, you can see here which effects are needed in the linear predictor to obtain the mean.  So for instance, post*Con is #2 and requires only the intercept while post*Trt is #4 and requires the intercept and "trtTrt" effect.  There are many resources for additional information about linear modeling of factors in general, and in R.

messages.subject: Re: BACI design in pcountOpen
parts:
I have another question related to my BACI design. Reminder that I have 4 primary sampling periods and 3 secondary (all point count data). Our treatments (timber harvests) were delayed at some sites. So, for instance, in KY I have 1 year pre and 3 years post, while most points in WV and at one VA site I have 2 years pre and 2 years post, and at the other VA site I have 3 years pre and 1 year post. I have attached my yearly site covariates "hvst" and "ysh" so you can visualize this.

I am most interested in estimating population growth rate or recruitment post-harvest. Specifically, I want to determine at what basal area do we get the biggest change in bird abundance. My questions are, do I have to model a subset of my data that only includes 1 year pre- and 1 year post-harvest since the VA data are the limiting factor here, which is what I did for the recent NAOC meeting? Or including yearly site covariates assures that the model knows to estimate gamma using only post-harvest data rather than just primary sampling periods 2-4?

Thank you so much!

Example of my models:

mF=pcountOpen(~site+asp+preba, ~plot+ysh+ba+I(ba^2)+site+dist.edge, 
              ~1, ~observe+noise, cerwumf, mixture=c("P"), K=50, dynamics=c("constant"),

messages.author: 1812cd2b1d8ede7e
messages.subject: Re: BACI design in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Gretchen and others,

I'd be very interested to hear folks' thoughts on this question as I had a very similar problem with a forestry project with treatments in different years at different sites.  My inclination is to include a interactive term of years-since-harvest X harvest-type (in my case clearcut, single-tree selection, etc), since it's predictable that responses with change through time as succession follows a timber harvest.  Not sure how that fits into unmarked modeling however.

Best,
Alex

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: BACI design in pcountOpen
parts:
You could create a "yearlySiteCov" that indicates if each primary period was "Before" or "After" the treatment. You could also treat primary period itself as either a continuous or discrete yearlySiteCov, which would allow you to assess trends or other types of temporal effects. Interactions of treatment and time are possible too.

Richard
